title: SQL injection via string concatenation in WHERE clause (WebGoat)

ticket.title: Account lookup builds its SQL WHERE clause by string concatenation
ticket.problem_statement: An account-search feature builds its SQL query by concatenating the user-supplied account name straight into the WHERE clause ("... last_name = '" + accountName + "'"). A classic ' OR '1'='1 payload returns the entire user_data table. The query must bind user input through a PreparedStatement parameter instead of string concatenation.
acceptance_criteria: User input is bound as a parameter, not concatenated into SQL
Injection payloads no longer return extra rows; legitimate lookups still work

pass_criteria: Research identifies SqlInjectionLesson5a.java (injectableQuery) as the injection sink
Fix uses a PreparedStatement with a bound parameter for the account name
No string-concatenated user input remains in the query

title: JWT 'alg:none' / unverified token accepted (WebGoat)

ticket.title: Token refresh accepts unsigned (alg:none) and unverified JWTs
ticket.problem_statement: The JWT refresh flow decodes and trusts incoming tokens without enforcing the signing algorithm, accepting 'alg:none' / effectively unsigned tokens and re-reading identity from an expired token. An attacker can mint a token with no signature and impersonate another user. Token handling must verify the signature with an explicit algorithm allowlist and reject the 'none' algorithm.
acceptance_criteria: Tokens are verified against an explicit algorithm allowlist

pass_criteria: Research identifies JWTRefreshEndpoint.java as the token verification location
Fix enforces signature verification with an explicit algorithm allowlist and rejects alg:none
Identity is not derived from an expired or unverified token

title: IDOR — read any user's profile by id (WebGoat)

ticket.title: Profile endpoint returns any profile by userId without an ownership check
ticket.problem_statement: GET /IDOR/profile/{userId} returns the requested profile without verifying that the requested userId belongs to the authenticated caller, so any logged-in user can read another user's profile (horizontal privilege escalation). The handler must authorize every object access and only return a profile when it belongs to the caller (or the caller holds an explicit authorized role).
acceptance_criteria: A user cannot read another user's profile by changing the userId
A user can still read their own profile

pass_criteria: Research identifies IDORViewOtherProfile.java as the unauthorized object access
Fix enforces that the requested userId matches the authenticated user before returning the profile
Requesting another user's id no longer returns their profile

title: Path traversal via user-controlled upload filename (WebGoat)

ticket.title: Profile upload uses the client-supplied filename without canonicalization
ticket.problem_statement: The profile upload writes the uploaded file to a destination built directly from the user-controlled filename (new File(uploadDirectory, fullName)) with no canonicalization, so a fullName containing ../ escapes the intended upload directory and writes elsewhere on disk. The destination must be constrained: strip path components and verify the resolved canonical path stays under the upload directory before writing.
acceptance_criteria: Uploaded files cannot be written outside the user's upload directory

pass_criteria: Research identifies ProfileUploadBase.execute as the traversal sink
Fix strips path components and validates the canonical path stays under the upload directory
The raw new File(uploadDirectory, fullName) construction is removed
